newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - More Korean deals get done.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - More Korean deals get done.

text.p: Asian debt markets were quiet Wednesday with just a couple of Korean issues enlivening trade.
Hyundai International Merchant Bank (HIMB) set a three-year US$70 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue via arranger Credit Lyonnais Hong Kong.
The certificates were launched at par to float at 50 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return is 66 basis points.
That was more than the all-in paid on HIMB's previous FRCD, which offered 61 basis points all-in to the top tier when launched in May.
But traders said the spread on the new issue still may not be wide enough to attract strong demand.

"HIMB usually is one of the weaker (merchant banks) and 66 is not enough for three years," said a secondary market trader. "You can easily get better names, like KMB and KIMB, for two, two and a half years, that pay 60-65 basis points," he said.
Korea International Merchant Bank in July launched a five-year FRCD with a three-year put option. That deal paid an all-in of 62 basis points.
A few weeks later Korea Merchant Banking Corp launched a three-year FRCD that also paid 62 basis points all-in.
Among other merchant banks, Asian Banking Corp and Saehan Merchant Bank both have mandated arrangers for upcoming fundraisings.

Korean corporate Newmax International officially launched its floating rate note issue through arrangers Korea First Finance and Nomura Securities. The notes are guaranteed by Nexmax Co and Taeil Media Co.
The five-year paper has a put option in year three and pays an all-in return of 137 basis points.
In the secondary market, traders said Guangdong Investments has been the big mover.
The Hong Kong-listed company is 38 percent held by Guangdong Enterprise Holdings, which is rated BB by Standard and Poor's Corp and Ba1 by Moody's Investors Service.
Guangdong Investment's floating rate notes pay a coupon of 140 basis points over the six-month LIBOR and, with fees, an all-in return of 170 basis points to the top tier.
Traders said that spread has narrowed significantly in the secondary market, tightening to about 150 basis points over LIBOR amid strong demand.
The deal had been heavily heavily oversubscribed in syndication and raised to US$100 million from US$80 million.
